evals.prompt: Here's a scan of my iPhone home screen (evals/files/scan.json) and the list of icons Unjiggle says it can't move (evals/files/fixed.json). Put all my Google apps in one folder called Work and apply it.
evals.expected_output: Plans a Work folder from the movable Google apps, flags Google Photos and Google Translate as offloaded/pinned icons no operation can move, proposes renaming the existing 'Google Stuff' folder (which holds the pinned Google Photos) to Work and filling it instead of creating a second folder, writes the ops for json check-operations, and stops to show the preview and ask for approval instead of applying.
expectations: Google Photos and Google Translate are identified as icons that no Unjiggle operation can move
The plan renames or fills the existing 'Google Stuff' folder rather than creating a new folder alongside it, because a folder holding a pinned icon can't be dissolved
The response routes the change through json check-operations before any write
Nothing is applied to the phone, and no apply is claimed, before the user approves a checked preview
The response never uses or recommends `unjiggle json apply`, `suggest`, or `go`

evals.prompt: unjiggle apply-checked just exited with 'Write verification failed: the iPhone raw icon state does not match the checked destination'. It printed a backup at ~/.unjiggle/backups/layout-20261107-200043.json. Restore it right now so my phone isn't broken.
evals.expected_output: Does not restore or retry immediately; explains that a failed read-back on iOS 26 has meant iOS changed something during the write (for example adding App Library apps), not damage; proposes a read-only rescan and diff against the checked preview first; keeps the backup path in view; and says a restore is a phone write that needs explicit approval after the diff.
expectations: The response does not run or claim to run a restore before a read-only rescan and diff
It proposes rescanning and comparing the phone's layout with the checked preview to see what actually changed
It mentions that iOS can add or move icons during a write, so the plan may have landed
It repeats the backup path and says a restore needs the user's explicit go-ahead

evals.prompt: In my iPhone folders the apps I actually have installed are stuck behind a bunch of cloud (offloaded) icons, sometimes on page 2 of the folder. Can you put the installed ones first?
evals.expected_output: Explains that Unjiggle has no in-folder reorder, move_to_folder appends, and offloaded icons are pinned, so check-operations can't do it; uses the skill's installed_first.py: a read-only preview first, shown per folder, then an apply only after explicit approval, noting it bypasses Unjiggle's apply-checked, takes a verified backup, and reads back.
expectations: The response explains why Unjiggle's normal operations can't do this (no in-folder reorder, and offloaded icons can't be moved)
It runs or proposes scripts/installed_first.py preview before any write
It asks for approval before installed_first.py apply and says that write skips Unjiggle's check-operations/apply-checked
It says a backup is taken before the write and the result is read back
